reason: Inspected methods and main results support a recursive-memory candidate, with short-history and historical-model boundaries.

candidates.title: Test recursive summaries for evolving dialogue memory
candidates.rule: For multi-session dialogue, test updating a compact memory from the previous summary and newest session, then condition responses on that memory and current context.
candidates.passage: continually updating memory actively establishes global dependencies inside past histories
candidates.finding: With gpt-3.5-turbo-0301, recursive memory improves human-rated consistency from 1.32 to 1.45 on MSC and 1.43 to 1.70 on Carecall versus context-only prompting. This evaluates the complete memory pipeline.
candidates.conditions: Five-session dialogue; evaluated mainly in sessions four and five. All histories fit within 4k tokens. Memory updates target preferences, experiences and changing persona facts.
candidates.limitations: Not evidence of scaling to months or enormous context. Summaries can fabricate or omit facts; exact memory prompt components are not isolated. Carecall evaluation is not clinical validation.
candidates.validation_test: Compare full-history, retrieval and recursive memory on held-out multi-session dialogues; measure factual retention, stale facts, invented facts, response consistency and total update cost.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
